thread:
Alice Turner: Heads up — seeing a three-way healthcheck flap across regions: eu -> us-west -> us-east. Customers reporting intermittent 503s and elevated latencies. Pager fired 2m ago. @oncall please triage.
Oncall Bot: PagerDuty incident PD12345 created and assigned to Maya Patel.
Maya Patel: I’m on it — joining. Any immediate mitigation?
Ben Cho: Repro: hitting primary model endpoints triggers health-check fail in eu, then traffic bounces to us-west, then us-east, then back. Looks like health-checks are oscillating early in the stack.
Sam Rodriguez: Logs show probe latency spikes and occasional 500 from the health-check handler. Skipping 3s window at 60s.
Ella Ng: Observability — we see increased kv-cache misses when traffic moves regions. Might be cold-cache cascade.
Maya Patel: Initial customer impact: ~4% of inference requests failing for a small set of long-tail tenants, likely those pinned to eu model variants.
Alice Turner: Customer note: enterprise-3 reported degraded UX; support loop opened.
Ben Cho: Quick mitigation option: disable cross-region fallback in routing-policies so requests stay in originating region until we stop flap. That avoids ping-pong.
Maya Patel: Agree. Plan: 1) Pause interregion fallback policy 2) Increase health-check grace to 30s 3) Roll back any recent model-variant routing changes.
Sam Rodriguez: Applying policy pause now — patching routing config.
Sam Rodriguez: ```sh
kubectl patch configmap routing-policies -n redwood -p '{"data":{"interregion_fallback":"disabled-temporary"}}'
# verify: curl -sS http://config-api.local/policies | jq .interregion_fallback
```
Oncall Bot: Routing policy interregion_fallback set to disabled-temporary by Sam Rodriguez.
Ben Cho: Health-check tune: bumping consecutive-failures threshold from 2 -> 5 and probe-interval 5s -> 15s. Applying to eu/us-west/us-east pools.
Ben Cho: ```yaml
health_check:
  interval_seconds: 15
  failure_threshold: 5
```
Maya Patel: Done. Monitoring for 10m. Please keep an eye on served model variant counts and KV cache miss rate.
Ella Ng: Metrics after policy pause: region failover events dropped to 0 in last 30s, error rate started trending down. KV-cache miss spike still present but decreasing as warm-up continues.
Alice Turner: Communicating to support: "We've paused inter-region fallback to stop routing oscillation. Engineers are tuning healthchecks and warming caches. Expect partial recovery within 10-15min."
PagerDuty Bot: PD12345 acknowledged by Maya Patel.
Maya Patel: Handing off to Ella for follow-up on cache warm-up and Sam for persistent fix on health-check handler. I'll update postmortem.
Ella Ng: Follow-up actions: run controlled warmup for eu cache and add proactive cache prefill for pinned tenants. Adding a temporary routing rule to route enterprise-3 to eu-only until caches warmed.
Sam Rodriguez: Root cause hypothesis: a regression in the health-check handler introduced a transient 500 when KV store returned a retryable error — the router marks region unhealthy too aggressively. Will open PR to add retry/backoff in health-check and add circuit-breaker around interregion fallback.
Maya Patel: Escalation note: no data exfil, no auth issues. Business impact low-medium but user-visible. Customers affected: enterprise-3 (major), three mid-market tenants, normal traffic otherwise.
Alice Turner: Timeline update for stakeholders: initial pager at T0, mitigation (policy pause + health-check tune) at T0+6m, measurable recovery T0+9m.
Ben Cho: Continuing to monitor. If oscillation returns, we’ll re-enable fallback + route to canary variant.
Maya Patel: Leaving this thread open for postmortem. Assigning owners: health-check fix = Sam, cache prefill + follow-up metrics = Ella, postmortem = Maya.
Oncall Bot: Incident PD12345 marked as "mitigated" by Maya Patel at T0+12m.
Alice Turner: Thanks everyone. Please add runbook updates: lower aggressiveness of health-check failures, add probe rate limits, and document interregion fallback toggle procedure. :thumbsup:
